note: Baseline of Swift compiler warnings that are ACCEPTED, each with the evidence for accepting it. Enforced by scripts/check-swift-warnings.mjs. Entries match on file + message pattern, deliberately NOT on line number, so ordinary edits above a warning do not invalidate the baseline. Any warning outside this list fails the build; an entry that matches nothing ALSO fails, so a warning that disappears (a toolchain fix, a rewrite) forces the entry to be removed rather than silently lingering.
verifiedWith: Apple Swift version 6.3.3 (swiftlang-6.3.3.1.3 clang-2100.1.1.101), swift-driver 1.148.6, target arm64-apple-macosx26.0

entries.messagePattern: 'catch' block is unreachable because no errors are thrown in 'do' block
entries.verdict: compiler false positive — the catch is live and load-bearing
evidence: BoundRegularFile.readAll DOES throw: PreparedImportActivator.swift:140-141 throws FileHashError.unreadable(errno: EFBIG) as soon as the running total would exceed the 64 KiB cap.
There is exactly one readAll declaration in the whole module (PreparedImportActivator.swift:128) — no shadowing overload, no protocol extension, no conditional compilation around it.

A minimal reproduction of the same shape (throwing method on a final class, local enum, nested non-throwing function, typed catch) compiles with NO warning, so the construct itself is not what triggers it.
The identical call shape at PreparedImportActivator.swift:567 (`do { data = try rec.readAll() }`) produces no warning in the same build.

DYNAMIC PROOF: MigrationCoordinatorTests.testOversizedOwnerRecordIsClassifiedMalformedNotRetriable drives a 64 KiB+1 owner record through inspectRecord and asserts the exact string 'owner record exceeds the size cap', which is produced at exactly one place — inside the catch in question. A catch a passing test walks through is not unreachable.
entries.whyNotSilenced: Deleting the catch to reach a zero-warning build would delete the EFBIG classification that turns an oversized owner record into .malformed instead of a retriable error — real handling in migration-safety code.
